standard_prerequisites: Polynomial algebra over a field: k[x] is a PID so (P, P') = (R); the derivative of a polynomial in characteristic p kills exactly the terms of degree divisible by p
core_obligations: Dichotomy: P' has degree < deg P, so a common divisor R of P and P' with (P, P') = (R) would be a nonconstant proper divisor of P if P and P' are not relatively prime - contradicting irreducibility; hence either gcd(P, P') = 1 or P' = 0
P' = 0 forces characteristic p: in characteristic 0 all coefficients would vanish, making P constant; in characteristic p it forces a_i = 0 whenever p does not divide i, so P(x) = P_1(x^p)
P_1 stays irreducible (a factorization of P_1 pulls back to one of P), and induction on the degree gives P(x) = Q(x^q) with q = p^f and gcd(Q, Q') = 1
proof_roadmap: Prove the dichotomy from the degree of the derivative
Analyze P' = 0 coefficient-wise to extract the p-th root substitution
Iterate by induction to reach the separable residual Q
